text:
sophia: noticed a weird spike in auth lockouts and repeated MFA prompts starting ~06:12 UTC — looks like a lot of the same orgs hitting 'approve' flows repeatedly. posting logs.
sec-bot: ALERT: suspicious_sso_retries detected for 14 users across 3 tenants (rate: 120/min). see /alerts/1755554321.
elaine: screenshots? any common client?
sophia: attaching a quick snippet from audit log: 
```
2026-01-11T06:11:58Z tenant=acme user=jdoe event=assertion_issued client=chrome_ext/1.4.2 ip=35.214.12.4 ua=Chrome/110.0 ext_id=com.calendar.sync
2026-01-11T06:12:03Z tenant=acme user=jdoe event=approval_flow_started ip=35.214.12.4 ua=Chrome/110.0
2026-01-11T06:12:06Z tenant=acme user=jdoe event=mfa_prompt_sent ip=35.214.12.4
2026-01-11T06:12:09Z tenant=acme user=jdoe event=assertion_issued ip=35.214.12.4 ua=Chrome/110.0 ext_id=com.calendar.sync
```
sophia: note ext_id repeated in ua; IP is same but we see rapid repeated assertion_issued for same user, then lockout triggers.
jamal: so not impossible-travel per se (same IP), but repeated assertion issuance could be a client misbehaving or an extension loop. any recent RBAC/KMS changes?
elaine: no RBAC churn this morning. KMS rotation was last week and successful, nothing in keyring logs.
devon: could be an OAuth refresh loop — extension opening auth window on every sync attempt and auto-submitting? if so, might be causing MFA fatigue.
sophia: support tickets already coming in from two customers claiming mass prompts.
ops-oncall: I’m paging the extension vendor contact (cc @devon) and putting a temporary rate-limit rule on auth endpoints for 10s per user per tenant. will also throttle approval page hits at the edge.
devon: can we add a quick mitigation: block the ext_id com.calendar.sync from anonymous grant flows while we investigate?
elaine: we can add a denylist at the WAF and drop any requests containing ext_id header or user-agent pattern. roll that in as an emergency rule.
sec-bot: mitigation applied: WAF rule 23314 - drop requests matching ext_id=com.calendar.sync. observed drop count: 482 in last 3m.
sophia: already seeing decreased MFA prompt rate in telemetry, nice.
jamal: we should also create an audit entry for the deny rule and inform legal/compliance — potential PII impact if prompts were being phished.
elaine: agreed. jasper@legal notified. can we collect a sample of the assertion payloads (redact PII) and a list of affected users for post-incident review?
devon: yes — will export assertion ids and scrub emails, put in secure bucket (kms=customer-managed).
ops-oncall: timeline for containment: 06:15 WAF rule up, 06:20 denylist confirmed, 06:27 client vendor reached out, 06:40 vendor released patch v1.4.3 to stop reauth loop.
sophia: next steps: 1) notify impacted customers with recommended steps (disable extension until patch), 2) add a health-check to detect >5 assertion/sec per user, 3) add ext_id to suspicious clients list for future throttles, 4) postmortem.
jamal: can product/console team add a per-tenant alert to show bursty assertion trends? that would help earlier detection.
elaine: tagging for postmortem: owners = sec-team (elaine, jamal), infra (devon), support (sophia). timeline doc: https://redwood.internal/incident/1755554321
sec-bot: CREATED incident-1755554321 | severity=medium | owner=@elaine
sophia: moving to incident channel for updates. thanks all. :thumbsup:
